topic.title: Topic
topic.question: What is this Reel mainly about: the subject the viewer learns about, is entertained by, or is sold? Judge the subject, not the tools the creator happens to use. Technology has three places: 'tech' when the technology itself is explained in depth (how it is built, who built it, what it can do, specs, features, launches, comparisons, coding); 'tech_tools' when an app, AI tool or phone or computer feature is used to get an everyday job done and shown step by step for beginners (AI assistants, productivity apps, automations, phone tips); editing photos or videos (including AI editors), filming and cameras -> photography_video; designing graphics, drawing and design tools -> art_design; study apps and setups -> learning_study; a fitness app workout -> fitness. In an ad or sponsored Reel, the topic is what is promoted, judged the same way (a phone's specs and features: tech; an AI tool shown doing a task for you: tech_tools; an AI video editor: photography_video). Work, news or policy inside one field belongs to that field: a nurse's shift, a doctor on health policy or medical school -> health_wellness; a chef's kitchen -> food_drink; a tech company's news -> tech. Pick career_work, news_politics or learning_study only for jobs, news or studying in general. Pick lifestyle_daily_life only when the creator's everyday life is the point and no other subject leads; pick 'other' only when no topic fits. When the speech is only song lyrics or background music, ignore it and judge from the caption and on-screen text.
